purpose: Source-derived inventory of subscription, checkout, billing event and provider-state surfaces relevant to cancellation, delinquency and refund policy review. This registry does not decide customer-facing policy, refund eligibility, cancellation timing, grace periods, proration, access entitlement, provider refund mechanics or legal terms.

technical_surfaces.technical_observation: The model can represent a trialing subscription and trial start/end timestamps; this does not define customer cancellation rights during trial or any conversion/refund rule.
policy_questions_for_real_review: When and how may a customer cancel during trial?
Does cancellation end access immediately or at a later reviewed boundary?
What customer notice is required before trial conversion or expiration?
What happens if billing credentials/provider activation are unavailable?

technical_surfaces.technical_observation: The model stores current billing-period boundaries and price interval/amount, but those timestamps do not themselves establish service-entitlement, cancellation-effect or refund policy.
policy_questions_for_real_review: Does paid access continue through current_period_end after cancellation?
Under what circumstances may access end earlier?
Are monthly and yearly cancellation/refund rules different?
How are price changes and effective periods disclosed to existing customers?

technical_surfaces.technical_observation: The schema can distinguish a cancellation-at-period-end flag and cancellation timestamp from terminal status, but no customer-facing cancellation rule is approved by these fields.
policy_questions_for_real_review: What action sets cancel_at_period_end and what confirmation must the customer receive?
Can a scheduled cancellation be reversed before the period ends?
What exact event moves a subscription to canceled?
Which customer-visible date represents the effective cancellation date?

technical_surfaces.technical_observation: The technical state can represent past_due/delinquency and authority-event transitions, but no grace period, retry cadence, suspension timing, recovery rule or communication obligation is approved here.
policy_questions_for_real_review: When does a failed/overdue payment become delinquent?
Is there a grace period, and if so who approves its duration?
What product access changes are allowed during delinquency?
What retry, recovery and customer-notification rules apply?
When may delinquency lead to cancellation?

technical_surfaces.technical_observation: A canceled subscription state and audit event trail exist technically, but terminal state does not prove why cancellation occurred, customer rights, refund eligibility or retention/deletion treatment.
policy_questions_for_real_review: Which causes may produce terminal cancellation?
What customer confirmation and effective date are required?
What happens to data and account access after cancellation?
Which retention/deletion policy dependency must be referenced?

technical_surfaces.technical_observation: Checkout intents can be pending/created/paid/expired/failed/canceled. These technical statuses do not establish that money moved, a refund occurred, or a customer cancellation right was exercised.
policy_questions_for_real_review: How are abandoned, expired, failed and canceled checkout attempts communicated?
How are duplicate or repeated payment attempts handled?
What evidence is required before treating a charge as paid?
How must any failed or duplicated charge dispute be escalated?

technical_surfaces.technical_observation: Webhook receipts support idempotent provider-event reconciliation. A receipt or event type is operational evidence only and cannot define refund/cancellation terms or provider financial truth without the authorized billing proof chain.
policy_questions_for_real_review: Which provider events are authoritative for payment, cancellation and refund state changes?
How are duplicate, late, ignored or failed webhook events handled?
What customer communication follows a material billing-state reconciliation?
Which operational receipts must be retained under the approved retention matrix?

technical_surfaces.technical_observation: The authority-event ledger can explain technical subscription transitions; it is not itself the customer contract, refund decision or legal approval record.
policy_questions_for_real_review: Which cancellation/refund/delinquency decisions require an authority event?
What source/reason values are necessary for audit without over-collecting customer data?
Which human or provider decisions require independent approval or receipt?
How long must this audit trail be retained?

technical_surfaces.technical_observation: Plan, price and fee-assumption metadata can support commercial calculation and versioning; it does not establish refund amount, proration, tax reversal, fee pass-through or customer disclosure policy.
policy_questions_for_real_review: Are refunds full, partial, prorated or unavailable under which reviewed circumstances?
How are taxes and provider fees treated in any refund calculation?
Which price/version applies when cancellation or refund is processed?
What disclosure is required for renewals and price changes?

technical_surfaces.technical_observation: Asaas is selected for BR V1 but remains selected_pending_credentials and not activated. No provider refund/cancellation API behavior, commercial term or production capability is proven by selection metadata.
policy_questions_for_real_review: Which provider-native cancellation/refund capabilities are actually available after real activation?
Which provider receipts are required for a real financial reversal?
What happens when customer policy requires an outcome that provider mechanics cannot complete automatically?
What provider fees, timing or operational constraints must be disclosed after real evidence review?
